lines.text: `pnpm eval -- --help` lists every flag. Cases live in `eval/cases/<id>/` (`case.json`, `expected.md`, frozen `sources/`). `eval/review-criteria.md` says how to read and write `expected.md`.
Producer and grader run in Muse Code (`muse exec`). Both default to `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`. Override with `--producer-model` or `--grader-model`.

Producer and grader run in Muse Code (`muse exec`). The producer defaults to `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`; the grader defaults to `muse-ember-1.0`. Override with `--producer-model` or `--grader-model`.

Muse Ember (`muse-ember-1.0`) grades by default because repeated rescore checks put it at parity for less time. It has no contributor variant, so the harness passes `--contributor-mode off` for it; with the mode on it fails with "does not exist or you lack access". Across five runs each on `comprehende-50` and `comprehende-57`, Ember-vs-Spark verdict agreement (median 50 of 52) overlapped Spark-vs-Spark (51 of 52), grader tokens matched at the median, no run failed to parse, and Ember graded about 3.7 times faster. The producer stays on Spark contributor: Ember spot checks wrote thinner reviews, and on the Model API Ember output costs $0.50 per 1M tokens against Spark contributor $0.20 (input $0.10 both; Ember bills the whole request at $0.30 input and $1.50 output over 200K input tokens).

lines.text: Runs use the `muse` CLI login (`muse login`), which spends the subscription, by default — even when `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY` is set. `--use-api-key` spends that key (pay as you go) instead. `--cli-login` names the default and wins over `--use-api-key`. CI writes the repo secret `MUSE_AUTH_JSON` (a CI-only device login, not your daily one) to `~/.config/muse/auth.json` and checks it with `muse usage`; only a missing secret falls back to `--use-api-key` with `MUSE_CODE_API_KEY` — a failed check keeps the subscription so a dead login fails visibly instead of silently spending API credit. Refresh an expired CI login by running `muse login` once in any Linux environment with a fresh `HOME` (a container works), then `gh secret set MUSE_AUTH_JSON < ~/.config/muse/auth.json`. Every Muse run passes `--contributor-mode on` and resolves a bare `muse-spark-*` id to its `-contributor` tier. The `muse` CLI must be on `PATH`. The eval workflow installs it. Locally, install the CLI the way `.github/workflows/eval.yml` does.

Refresh an expired CI login by running `muse login` once in any Linux environment with a fresh `HOME` (a container works), then `gh secret set MUSE_AUTH_JSON < ~/.config/muse/auth.json`. Every Muse run resolves a bare `muse-spark-<version>` id to its `-contributor` tier and passes `--contributor-mode on` for that tier and for `muse-wonder` ids, which Muse Code offers in either mode; other ids, such as `muse-spark-1.3-turbo` and `muse-ember-1.0`, stay unchanged and get `--contributor-mode off`, because they have no contributor variant. The `muse` CLI must be on `PATH`. The eval workflow installs it. Locally, install the CLI the way `.github/workflows/eval.yml` does.
